promises.quote: The Ministry of Justice will respond directly to the Coroner on this.
promises.summary: Ministry of Justice to address unauthorised alcohol production.

promises.quote: Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (SPFT) undertook a Root Cause Analysis Investigation following Mr Haines death and three recommendations were made: a. healthcare staff should be trained in how to detect diabetes and hypertension; b. long term conditions such as diabetes and hypertension are managed in line with National Institute for Care Excellence (NICE) guidelines; and c. reviews of repeat medication comply with NICE
promises.summary: SPFT implemented diabetes and hypertension training for staff.

promises.quote: An on-going action plan remains in place and will continue to be monitored closely for the remainder of the trust's contract which ends on 31 March 2020. To support · this, and ensure a reduction in any risk to patients, commissioners have appointed a clinical reviewer (previously Director of Nursing
promises.summary: Commissioners appointed clinical reviewer to oversee care at HMP Lewes weekly.

promises.quote: The Prison and Healthcare providers have reminded staff of the protocols in relation to responding to an unresponsive body, including the need for prison staff to elicit a verbal or non-verbal response from each prisoner when cells are unlocked. Further reminders have been issued on the need to immediately call an ambulance when a Code RED or Code BLUE is called, including a new poster in the control room.
promises.summary: Protocols for responding to unresponsive bodies reinforced with staff training.

promises.quote: Electronic Patient Records All healthcare providers are given access to electronic healthcare software, SystmOne. Substance misuse services have their own database which records performance and on which payment is based. Clinical information is recorded on SystmOne.
promises.summary: Implementation of SystmOne electronic patient records across providers.

The failure to carry out diagnostic testing and monitoring for his diabetes and to confirm his considerable cardiovascular disease
concerns.hazard: missed diabetes monitoring and cardiovascular disease confirmation

concerns.quote: The standard of care appears to have fallen well below that which he could have received in the community
There were no protocols or agreements between healthcare staff and the prison service as to how best to respond to an unresponsive body
concerns.hazard: absence of response protocols for unresponsive inmates

concerns.quote: There is no system to ensure that important healthcare information including recent administration of medicines and the results of physical observations is passed between separate providers of healthcare in the criminal justice system at the time a person is conveyed between the police, the court and the prison.
concerns.hazard: lack of information transfer between healthcare providers

concerns.quote: There is no standard medical records system which can be accessed by each healthcare organisation to ensure the efficient and effective transfer of medical information.
concerns.hazard: absence of standard medical records system

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of effective communication or information transfer between separate healthcare providers involved in custodial settings. The earlier report notes missing protocols between prison health teams, while the later report describes no system for passing medical details during transfers between police, court, and prison.
